energy_balance: PV 1.64 kWp x 3.0-5.5 PSH x PR 0.70-0.75 = about 3.4-6.8 kWh/day (about 5 kWh typical dry season, about 3.5 monsoon). Load 2.2 kW shaft /0.88/0.97 = 2.58 kW electrical (1.8-2.6 kW over the 40-60 kg/h range); demand at 4-7 h = 7-18 kWh/day. Usable battery about 4.3-4.9 kWh only shifts energy within a day (first day from full: about 3.5-4 h). Standby 45 mA x 51 V is about 2.3 W, negligible. Sustained run time about 1.3-3.9 h/day, about 2-2.5 h at full load in good sun. Annual: about 1.64 x 1,500 x 0.75 = about 1,850 kWh, so at most about 700-850 full-load h/yr against the claimed 1,000-1,400 h. Energy budget does not close; roughly 40-55% of claimed output. Both reviews reach this correctly.
verdict: A is modestly better (38/46 vs 35/46). Both reach the same correct, well-supported verdict (do not build as drawn; resize the energy system, then redesign battery packaging, enclosure thermal and stones). Neither has wrong calculations or harmful advice. A also catches pulley retention, panel soiling mitigation, the controller-dependent E-stop/guarding hazard and flour-temperature tripping. B adds a stronger parked-wind overturning check, SPD/fuse sizing, dry-running/restart, phase-cable ampacity and better storage wiring. The difference is real but small.
